question: What is a fomite in the context of contact infections?

options.A: An insect vector that transmits tropical diseases
options.B: A specialized white blood cell fighting bacteria
options.C: A chemical used to sterilize surgical instruments
options.D: A non-living object that harbors infectious agents

explanation: Fomites are inanimate surfaces or objects like door handles and shared clothing that transfer pathogens between hosts. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h1)

question: Indirect contact transmission differs from direct contact because it involves what?

options.A: Blood-sucking vectors like mosquitoes and ticks
options.B: Airborne droplet nuclei traveling long distances
options.C: Ingestion of contaminated municipal water supplies
options.D: An intermediate non-living object or surface

explanation: Indirect spread relies on fomites to bridge the physical gap between the infected source and the new host. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h1)

question: Scabies is a classic example of which type of transmission?
explanation: Scabies mites burrow into the skin and transfer directly from one person's skin to another during close contact. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h2)

question: Why is environmental surface cleaning vital for controlling indirect contact infections?

options.A: Cleaning prevents vectors from breeding inside hospital wards
options.B: Pathogens survive on fomites and wait for a new host
options.C: Chemical disinfectants destroy airborne spores instantly
options.D: Wiping surfaces stops droplet nuclei from spreading further

explanation: Indirect infections spread because germs linger on inanimate objects, making regular disinfection necessary to break the chain. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h2)

question: Which bacterium is most commonly responsible for skin boils and wound infections?
explanation: Staphylococcus aureus lives on human skin and frequently causes purulent soft tissue infections and boils. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h3)

question: What environmental condition in tropical regions encourages the spread of fungal skin infections?

options.A: Low atmospheric pressure at high altitudes
options.D: Prolonged exposure to dry desert winds

explanation: Fungi flourish in warm and moist environments, making tropical climates ideal for dermatophyte growth and skin irritation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h3)

question: Why does scabies infestation cause intense itching, especially at night?

options.A: Fungal spores releasing histamines into the bloodstream
options.B: Allergic reactions to burrowed mites and their waste
options.C: Viral replication peaking during dark hours
options.D: Bacterial toxins destroying deep muscle tissues

explanation: The body mounts an immune response against the protein waste and eggs left by mites under the skin, causing severe pruritus. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h4)

question: A patient with a primary fungal skin infection develops pus and increased pain. What has likely happened?

options.A: The fungus has transformed into a virus
options.B: Normal systemic reaction to anti-fungal drugs
options.D: Spontaneous healing of the original lesion

explanation: Breaking the skin barrier through scratching allows resident skin bacteria like staphylococci to enter and cause secondary infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h4)

question: What bedside procedure helps confirm a suspected fungal skin infection?

options.A: Complete blood count with differential analysis
options.C: Chest X-ray to check for pulmonary infiltrates
options.D: Urinalysis using a standard reagent strip

explanation: Treating skin scrapings with KOH dissolves keratinocytes and leaves fungal elements visible under microscopic examination. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h5)

question: Why is a wound swab for culture and sensitivity ordered before starting antibiotics?

options.A: To determine how long the patient has been sick
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of hospital admission
options.C: To identify the exact pathogen and effective drugs
options.D: To measure the patient's red blood cell volume

explanation: Culture and sensitivity testing pinpoints the causative microorganism and reveals which specific antimicrobial agents will cure the infection. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h5)

question: Which medication is standard first-line treatment for a scabies infestation?
explanation: Permethrin is a safe and effective topical scabicide that kills both the mites and their eggs when applied correctly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h6)

question: What non-pharmacological step is essential when treating a family member for scabies?

options.A: Washing all shared bed linen and clothes in hot water
options.B: Stopping all fluid intake for twenty-four hours
options.C: Isolating the infected person in a dark room for a month
options.D: Applying heavy makeup over the affected skin lesions

explanation: Mites can survive briefly on fabrics, so laundering clothing and bedding in hot water prevents immediate reinfection from fomites. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h6)

question: What is the single most effective way to stop cross-contamination in healthcare settings?

options.A: Wearing sterile face masks all day
options.C: Restricting all visitors from the ward

explanation: Handwashing or using alcohol rub removes transient microorganisms acquired from patients and contaminated surfaces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h7)

question: Which personal protective equipment is required when entering a room under contact precautions?
explanation: Contact precautions require barriers like gloves and gowns to prevent direct skin contact with the patient and contaminated environmental surfaces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h7)

question: Why should nurses engage local community leaders when planning public health campaigns?

options.A: To secure direct financial grants from international donors
options.B: To gain local trust and encourage community participation
options.C: To punish families who refuse to follow medical advice
options.D: To bypass government health policies and protocols

explanation: Community leaders hold influence and help bridge the gap between healthcare workers and local residents, ensuring better acceptance of health education. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h8)

question: Which educational message is most important for preventing the spread of fungal ringworm in schools?

options.A: Take strong oral antibiotics every morning
options.B: Wear heavy woolen sweaters in hot weather
options.C: Avoid sharing personal items like combs and towels
options.D: Wash hands only after eating meals

explanation: Fungal skin and scalp infections spread easily through shared grooming tools, hats, and clothing among school children. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h8)
